name: Ovarian Fibroma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Ovarian Fibroma

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of spindle-shaped fibroblastic cells with collagen production in ovarian tissue
Ultrasound showing a solid, hypoechoic, well-circumscribed ovarian mass
Presence of adnexal mass with or without pelvic discomfort

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus supportive imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Definitive diagnosis requires histopathological examination; imaging and clinical features guide preoperative suspicion.

laboratory: Normal tumor markers (CA-125 usually normal or mildly elevated)
imaging: Ultrasound: solid, hypoechoic, well-circumscribed ovarian mass
MRI: low signal intensity on T2-weighted images consistent with fibrous tissue
CT scan: solid ovarian mass, sometimes with ascites
genetic: No known specific genetic mutations associated with isolated ovarian fibroma
other: Histopathology: spindle cells with collagen bundles, absence of atypia
Meigs syndrome triad: ovarian fibroma, ascites, and pleural effusion

distinguishingFeatures: Thecomas are hormonally active causing estrogenic symptoms
Histology shows lipid-laden theca cells rather than fibroblasts
Malignant features on histology with cellular atypia and mitotic figures
Smooth muscle origin with spindle cells positive for smooth muscle actin

redFlags: Rapid increase in size of ovarian mass
Signs of malignancy such as weight loss or ascites with elevated tumor markers
references: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Ovarian Cancer Including Fallopian Tube Cancer and Primary Peritoneal Cancer
WHO Classification of Tumours of Female Reproductive Organs, 5th Edition, 2020
